tasks.short: Create and lay out drill and blast patterns

steps.what: Develop drill and blast patterns from site conditions and the agreed design constraints
Check the proposed designs against the site and lay out the approved pattern

tasks.design: Retain human development and site checking of the pattern, using {DOCS} for the existing design references. The reader's check authorises their layout work only; it does not replace any separate blasting design approval or permission to fire.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on geology, surroundings and the consequences of each proposed layout.
tasks.enabler_now: No grounded change removes the site-specific design and checking in this task.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling incomplete subsurface knowledge with the site's exclusion and damage constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The driller can compare the proposal with actual ground and stop when conditions differ.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in design responsibility or permission to perform blasting.

reach.task: Explain unresolved pattern and site concerns
reach.learn: Design review boundaries and site escalation procedure

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: site-specific drill and blast design and layout require competent judgement; the digest's billing tools do not demonstrate this task.

assumptions: Boundary is the driller's pattern development and layout; explosive handling, firing and independent specialist approval are separate work and earn no saving.

The driller checks survey reference, observed ground conditions, hole positions, spacing, depths, nearby assets and unresolved constraints in s1 and s2. These are human-produced design inputs, not an assumed structured safe-to-blast flag.
Where survey provenance or site conditions are uncertain, the driller stops layout and seeks the responsible specialist; missing data is not inferred.
Existing document or design tools are used before considering custom software. No new configuration or process is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Who is competent and authorised to design and approve each pattern
Existing design tools and independent approval procedure
research_questions: Is there separately measurable repetitive drafting after the design is settled, rather than design judgement itself?

already_counted.description: Develop, check and lay out the pattern

approvals.approved_version: Exact layout design revision, survey reference and observed site conditions checked before the driller's layout action; changes require rechecking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Both routine layouts and changed ground conditions retain full human design and site checking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review drilling feasibility and prepare cost estimates

steps.what: Review client requirements and proposed locations to define feasible drilling methods and estimate inputs
Calculate cost estimates from the selected method, quantities, resources and current rates
Check feasibility and cost assumptions, then issue the estimate with its limitations

tasks.design: Configure the existing {SPREADSHEET} estimate workbook to extend checked quantities and rates and show assumptions explicitly. The driller still reviews requirements and location feasibility, tests the cost basis and decides what estimate can be issued through {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Arithmetic and repeated rate entry can distract from checking site assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Protected formulas and versioned input tables can handle repeat calculations without judging whether drilling is feasible.
tasks.still_hard: Predicting ground response, access constraints, productive time and the scope of contingencies.
tasks.human_edge: The driller recognises assumptions that look numerically valid but do not fit the site.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic; no additional authority to accept uncertain ground conditions or contractual risk.

reach.task: Provide a traceable drilling estimate with assumptions
reach.learn: Rate provenance, exclusions and estimate version control

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: configured quantity-times-rate calculations can support drilling estimates; the feasibility decision remains human and the saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers the driller's review and estimate, excluding sales negotiation and subsequent drilling execution.

The driller produces method, hole count, depths, expected productive hours, equipment, consumable quantities, access constraints and contingency assumptions in s1. Capture and checking remain at full time. Unknown quantities cause a qualified estimate or manual investigation, not generated defaults.
An estimating owner supplies rate item, unit, currency, rate, validity date and scope. Extra rate-table maintenance is counted as other-role upkeep; the driller verifies applicability in s3.
Test the existing workbook or native estimating configuration first. Missing rates or incompatible units stop the calculation and use manual estimation in s3.
Only repeated arithmetic loses time; site review, feasibility judgement and issue checks retain their shares. Existing formula runtime is not labour.
unknowns: Who maintains reliable equipment and labour rates
research_questions: Does a timed estimate sample show manual arithmetic that can be removed without changing feasibility review time?

already_counted.description: Review the site, produce inputs and check and issue the estimate

incremental.description: Maintain rate validity and calculation controls

approvals.approved_version: Exact estimate revision, quantities, rate-table version, feasibility assumptions and exclusions; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R80 gives gross20, less focal upkeep7 gives net13. Range0-3 assumes most calculation is already formula-driven and only occasional repeated arithmetic is removed; site review remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Establish well conditions and pumping requirements, selecting the calculation cases and design constraints
Calculate pumping duty and losses for the checked hydraulic cases using the design calculator
Evaluate pumping system options and verify the selected design against actual well conditions

tasks.design: Configure the existing hydraulic design calculator in {OTHER} to rerun explicit, checked cases and record its results in {DOCS}. The driller still determines the design basis, judges pump suitability and refers decisions beyond their competence for specialist review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated numerical case setup and calculation can obscure the assumptions behind a pumping design.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing hydraulic calculators can run defined cases consistently without inventing well characteristics.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a credible design basis, interpreting well tests and addressing equipment limitations.
tasks.human_edge: The driller can challenge a mathematically consistent design that is unsuitable for the actual well.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated numerical work; system selection and competence limits remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain the design duty and unresolved installation constraints
reach.learn: Hydraulic units, equipment curves and review handoffs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a configured hydraulic calculator can rerun defined cases, but it does not establish well properties or validate pump suitability.

assumptions: Boundary is the driller's pumping design work, excluding obtaining well test measurements, equipment installation and specialist approval. No outside work is reduced or newly transferred.

The driller captures required flow, well levels, drawdown basis, pipe lengths, diameters, material, elevations, units and operating cases in s1, checking them against test and site evidence. Its full time includes capture and manual correction.

OTHER means the hydraulic design calculator. A competent design owner supplies the accepted calculation method and equipment data; added method and data upkeep is charged to other_role. No free structured suitability flag is assumed.
Test native case configuration first. Missing measurements, incompatible units or cases beyond the validated method stop automatic calculation and return to manual assessment in s3.
Only manual case arithmetic is removed; existing solver runtime earns no saving. The driller's gate is their own design submission, not unrestricted engineering approval.
unknowns: Whether routine calculations are already automatic
The driller's actual design competence and approval boundary
Available well tests and equipment data
research_questions: Can a controlled repeat-case trial remove numerical handling while preserving full design-basis and equipment checks?

already_counted.description: Establish hydraulic inputs and evaluate and check the design

incremental.description: Investigate calculation exceptions and verify changed case setups
Maintain accepted calculation methods and equipment data

approvals.approved_version: Exact design revision, hydraulic input cases, calculation version and equipment selection checked for submission; any change requires renewed checking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gives gross25, less focal upkeep8 gives net17. Range0-4 assumes a small minority of cases need repeated manual numerical handling and existing calculators already do most work; selection judgement remains full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Signal crane operators during equipment moves

steps.what: Observe the equipment move and signal crane operators, stopping when the situation becomes unclear

tasks.design: Keep live observation and signalling with the competent person at the move. No record in {DOCS} substitutes for seeing current positions and maintaining effective communication.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task is a live coordination action with changing physical conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No grounded software change removes the need for direct observation and clear signals.
tasks.still_hard: Maintaining communication and noticing people, obstructions and changes in visibility.
tasks.human_edge: The signaller can stop immediately when actual conditions differ from the plan.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in signalling responsibility or movement authority.

reach.task: Coordinate clear stop and movement signals
reach.learn: Agreed signals, visibility limits and stop procedure

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: crane signalling requires live physical coordination; no task labour reduction is supported by the supplied digest.

assumptions: Boundary is the driller's live signalling, excluding crane operation and lift planning; their labour is neither included nor reduced.

The driller directly observes equipment position, people, obstructions, visibility and acknowledgement during s1. No structured clear-path or safe-move input is assumed; unclear conditions cause a stop and manual clarification.
Existing communication arrangements are used. Native records may document the plan but no additional software configuration is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep follows from introducing no new tool, integration or process.
unknowns: Which person is assigned and competent to signal each movement
research_questions: Is there any separate repetitive administration in this task beyond the live signalling?

already_counted.description: Observe and signal throughout equipment movement

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Routine movement and poor-visibility stop situations both retain full live observation and signalling time.

role.altitude: Use checked calculation cases where repetitive arithmetic exists while retaining field design judgement and live signalling.
reach: Provide estimators with traceable drilling assumptions
Explain pumping design constraints to installation supervisors
role.ambitious_version: An earth driller whose repeat calculations are traceable and whose site judgement and physical coordination remain fully resourced.
